title: Verifier‑Grounded Evaluation of LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: A Preregistered NetConfig‑Semantic Study
abstract: We report a preregistered, fully archived, verifier‑grounded paired experiment (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1, preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) that compared a deterministic template baseline to a single‑pass LLM generator (declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini) on 120 synthetic intent→configuration tasks. The confirmatory design used a shared canonical candidate per pair for seed_0 (generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate"), supplied to both baseline and guarded scoring episodes. Using a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) we observed baseline = 120/120 verifier passes and guarded (gpt‑5‑mini, seed_0) = 120/120; paired difference = 0.00, 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729); McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. These artifact‑grounded outcomes are reported verbatim and traced to preregistered shared‑candidate semantics and templated task synthesis rather than to evidence of independent LLM robustness. We release the full execution and validation bundle (execution/*), provide exact artifact paths and SHA‑256 hashes for audit, and recommend artifact‑anchored follow‑ups (independent per‑condition sampling, multi‑seed sensitivity, validator diversity, broader task heterogeneity) to measure independent generative reliability.

sections.introduction: Modern network operations increasingly investigate natural‑language intent → device configuration workflows driven by generative models. While LLMs promise operator productivity, operational correctness (reachability, access control equivalence, BGP policy preservation, ordering/transient safety) is essential prior to deployment. Prior work argues for verifier grounding and generate–validate–repair patterns to avoid silent semantic errors [doi:10.1145/3603269.3604866]. We preregistered a narrowly scoped confirmatory experiment to answer the following research question: Under a preregistered verifier‑grounded paired protocol, does a single‑pass LLM generator yield a lower verifier pass rate than a deterministic template baseline on synthetically generated NetOps intent→configuration tasks? Our contributions are: (1) a frozen, machine‑readable preregistration (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; SHA‑256 7db1663c...) and full execution/validation artifact bundle; (2) an exact, artifact‑traced report of the confirmatory outcome (both conditions 120/120) and the concrete artifact causes (shared canonical candidates and templated tasks); and (3) concrete, artifact‑grounded recommendations and re‑run pathways for informative independent generative evaluations.
sections.related_work: Verifier‑grounded NetOps analysis and intent→configuration research motivate our methodology. Batfish and its evolution demonstrate the practical value of high‑fidelity configuration validators for pre‑deployment checks and their role in diagnosis and automation [doi:10.1145/3603269.3604866]. Recent intent‑driven configuration and LLM→NetOps works stress the importance of semantic correctness over token metrics and motivate paired designs with validators [doi:10.23919/cnsm62983.2024.10814407, doi:10.1002/nem.70029]. Our study differs by delivering a preregistered, fully hashed execution record and by diagnosing a degenerate confirmatory outcome with explicit artifact provenance rather than introducing new models or fabricated results.
sections.methodology: Design and preregistration. The preregistration (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; SHA‑256 7db1663c...) specified: N=120 programmatic tasks (40 per topology class: edge, datacenter, multi‑AS); two conditions (baseline deterministic template, guarded LLM); primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory seed_0 semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (the identical canonical candidate was supplied to both conditions per pair). The preregistration also pre‑specified exploratory multi‑seed sampling (seeds_1..4) for later sensitivity analyses and contamination heuristics (exact match / normalized 5‑gram ≥0.95 → suspected_contamination). Model and orchestration. Declared model: gpt‑5‑mini via adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1; full model config archived at execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Validator. We used a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, version 5.0). The validator parses normalized configurations, enforces workflow and intent constraints from the task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl), evaluates final state and transient safety, and emits binary pass/fail plus a detailed validator_trace per episode (examples: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json). Execution contract and accounting. Execution was run in scientific_confirmatory mode under hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Planned_episode_count = 240 (two episodes per pair), completed_episode_count = 240, model_calls_used = 120 (shared_initial canonical candidate per pair), maximum_model_calls = 240. All provider call traces and per‑episode hashes are archived (execution/provider_calls/*.json; execution/responses/*.txt; full manifest and per‑file SHA‑256 hashes included in execution artifact manifest). Scoring rules and inference. Each episode used scorer deterministic_netops_validator_v5 with scoring_rule full_intent_constraint_validation (scoring outputs archived under execution/scoring/*.json). Confirmatory inference followed the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1: paired estimator = mean(llm_i − baseline_i) over i=1..120; McNemar exact two‑sided test and 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed=1729) were computed. Contamination and reproducibility. Preregistered contamination heuristics were executed and archived (analysis/contamination_summary.csv). The immutable initial master prompt is included in provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). All artifacts, seeds, code, and hashes required to reproduce the run are released with the bundle (see deterministic_reconciliation.json and execution manifest references).
sections.results: Execution and validator outcomes. All confirmatory episodes completed: complete_pair_count = 120, failed_episode_count = 0. Validator pass counts: baseline_success_count = 120/120 (100%), guarded_success_count (gpt‑5‑mini, seed_0) = 120/120 (100%). Paired contingency table: n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 9f25790c...). Paired estimate = 0.00. Bootstrap inference (10,000 resamples, seed=1729): 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00]. McNemar exact two‑sided p = 1.0. Representative artifact evidence. The shared canonical candidate usage is visible in execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e1e36...) and in the corresponding scoring trace execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 0d56c1add7c5a57f...). Deterministic reconciliation. The deterministic_reconciliation.json records provider call accounting, cache statistics (cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 120), and condition counts; all accounting checks passed (all_deterministic_consistency_checks_passed = true). Contamination heuristics. analysis/contamination_summary.csv (SHA‑256 389227f0...) contains the results of preregistered overlap checks; no confirmatory flags under preregistered thresholds were found. Interpretation of the numeric outcome. The observed degenerate agreement is mechanically correct for the executed pipeline (identical canonical supplied candidates) but uninformative about independent per‑condition generative reliability. The collapsed bootstrap CI and McNemar p=1.0 are direct mathematical consequences of identical paired binary outcomes (n_11 = N).
sections.discussion: Artifact‑grounded diagnosis. The confirmatory degeneracy arises from three artifact‑documented, preregistered causes: (1) Confirmatory generation semantics: for seed_0 the preregistered generation_semantics was "shared_initial_candidate" and the execution bundle shows the same canonical candidate supplied to both baseline and guarded episodes (execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt examples: SHA‑256 8f38c8be..., ae967f70..., f7f4db24...). (2) Task synthesis regularity: programmatic task templates encode required_sequence and tight workflow policies (execution/task_manifest.jsonl entries), producing narrow valid solution forms that template‑aligned candidates satisfy. (3) Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces the same constraints used to synthesize reference answers, increasing the probability that canonical candidates validate. Consequences for evaluation practices. A confirmatory paired test that reuses identical candidates per pair reliably detects differences only when per‑pair candidates differ; it is not a test of independent LLM generative robustness. To obtain informative comparisons we propose artifact‑anchored protocol changes (all available to re‑run using the bundled code): (A) independent_per_condition sampling for confirmatory comparisons (remove shared_initial reuse); (B) multi‑seed sampling per condition (pre‑registered exploratory seeds_1..4) and explicit seed‑sensitivity statistics; (C) task heterogeneity expansion beyond templated sequences (introduce randomized intent paraphrases and extra constraints); (D) validator diversity: combine deterministic validator with control‑plane emulation or reachability analyzers to increase construct validity; (E) multi‑model comparisons to quantify model variance. Reproducibility and audit. Every key file, provider call trace, scoring trace, and summary artifact is included in the execution bundle with SHA‑256 per‑file hashes (execution manifest). Representative artifact paths and hashes: execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 a40e96e212ab87da...), execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 8f38c8be...), execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 0d56c1ad...), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 9f25790c...). These enable exact reproduction of the reported run. On contamination: the preregistered string‑overlap heuristics were applied and archived (analysis/contamination_summary.csv); while no flags were raised under the chosen thresholds, absence of a flag is not proof of zero training‑data exposure and we retain explicit residual uncertainty.
sections.conclusion: We executed the preregistered verifier‑grounded paired experiment and report the exact artifact‑verified outcome: under preregistered shared_initial_candidate confirmatory semantics both the deterministic template baseline and the recorded gpt‑5‑mini guarded condition validated on the N=120 synthetic tasks (both 120/120). This degenerate agreement is attributable to the preregistered shared‑candidate design and templated task synthesis, not to evidence that LLMs are universally reliable under independent sampling or realistic operational heterogeneity. We release the full execution, scoring, and analysis artifacts and provide concrete, artifact‑anchored recommendations and runnable changes to obtain informative independent generative comparisons (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed sensitivity, validator diversity, and broader task heterogeneity). The artifact bundle (execution/*, analysis/*, deterministic_reconciliation.json, provenance/master_prompt.txt) contains the exact inputs, outputs, traces, and SHA‑256 hashes needed for reproducible audit and re‑execution.

No human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Confirmatory generation semantics and provenance: the preregistered confirmatory runs used generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" for seed_0; the execution artifacts show the same canonical shared_initial candidate was supplied to both the baseline and guarded scoring episodes for each pair (representative artifacts: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218..., execution/responses/task-000002-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 ae967f70dfb6ccb8b5dbcb1491775f30...). limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: tasks were programmatically synthesized from deterministic templates and transformation rules; this favors regular solution forms and limits generality to heterogeneous operational intents.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair for seed_0; this reduces independence between conditions and explains the degenerate paired outcome (evidence: execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 examples: 8f38c8be..., ae967f70...).

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary design used one canonical seed per task (seed_0) for the paired analysis; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses are not part of the confirmatory inference reported here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces the same semantic constraints used to synthesize reference answers, increasing the probability that template‑aligned candidates validate and limiting construct validity for open operational distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: exact proof that the model was not exposed to template artifacts during pretraining cannot be provided; preregistered contamination heuristics (analysis/contamination_summary.csv SHA‑256 389227f0...) found no flags, but absence of flags is an imperfect proxy.

Single‑model, single‑validator result: findings apply to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded execution conditions and validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); they do not generalize to other LLM families, agentic pipelines, or different validators.
